title: Bajaj Auto Buyback: Understanding Your Capital Gains Tax

faq.a: A share buyback is when a company repurchases its own shares from the open market or from its shareholders. It's a way for companies to return cash to shareholders, reduce the number of outstanding shares, and potentially boost earnings per share.

faq.q: How has the taxation of buybacks changed recently?
faq.a: Effective April 1, 2026, the tax liability for buyback proceeds from listed shares shifts from the company (which previously paid DDT) to the individual shareholder. Shareholders now pay capital gains tax on the profit.

faq.q: Is the ₹1 lakh LTCG exemption still applicable to buyback gains?
faq.a: Yes, the exemption of the first ₹1 lakh of Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) from the sale of listed equity shares (where STT is paid) under Section 112A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, remains applicable to gains from buybacks.

faq.q: Do NRIs pay tax on buyback proceeds?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) tendering shares in a buyback are also subject to capital gains tax in India. The rates for STCG and LTCG are generally the same as for residents, but specific TDS provisions may apply.

faq.q: What is the significance of the holding period for buyback shares?
faq.a: The holding period determines whether your gain is short-term (held for 12 months or less, taxed at 15%) or long-term (held for more than 12 months, taxed at 10% above ₹1 lakh exemption).

faq.q: What if I incur a loss in the buyback?
faq.a: If your buyback proceeds are less than your cost of acquisition, you incur a capital loss. This loss can be set off against other capital gains in the same financial year or carried forward to be set off in future years as per income tax rules.

faq.q: How do I report buyback gains in my income tax return?
faq.a: You will need to report the capital gains from the buyback under the head "Capital Gains" in your Income Tax Return (ITR) form for the relevant assessment year. It's advisable to consult a tax professional for accurate filing.
